title: The Briefing
tagline: AI intelligence for Gauntlet AI — May 10, 2026

items.headline: OpenAI Launches GPT-5.5 Instant with 52.5% Fewer Hallucinations
items.summary: OpenAI rolled out GPT-5.5 Instant as the default ChatGPT model, reducing hallucinated claims by 52.5% on high-stakes prompts in medicine, law, and finance. The model improves image analysis, STEM reasoning, and includes memory sources—a transparency feature showing which past chats, files, or Gmail context shaped responses.

items.headline: White House Plans FDA-Style AI Model Vetting System
items.summary: The Trump administration is preparing an executive order to create a vetting system for new AI models, modeled on FDA drug approval processes. The move follows Anthropic's disclosure that its Mythos model can identify network vulnerabilities. Commerce Department expanded voluntary testing program with Google, Microsoft, and xAI providing government early access.

items.headline: Anthropic Releases 10 Agent Templates for Finance
items.summary: Anthropic released agent templates handling labor-intensive financial work: pitchbook building, KYC document screening, ledger reconciliation, and monthly close. Templates available as Claude Cowork/Code plugins or Managed Agents cookbooks. Claude now integrates Excel, PowerPoint, Word, and Outlook with automatic context transfer. Added 8 new data connectors including Dun & Bradstreet and Moody's MCP.

items.headline: Big Pharma Pours Billions into AI Despite Limited Drug Breakthroughs
items.summary: Eli Lilly, Roche, GSK, and AstraZeneca investing billions in AI partnerships, but clinical trial success rates haven't improved. Real wins come from manufacturing optimization—Eli Lilly used AI to improve tirzepatide production with 'mind blowing' output gains. Recursion cut experimental drug design from 4 years to 18 months; Takeda's AI-discovered psoriasis pill heading to FDA. RBC estimates $90B in potential 5-year US pharma savings, mostly from efficiency.

items.headline: Google DeepMind London Votes to Unionize Over Military AI Concerns
items.summary: DeepMind's London office voted to unionize (Communication Workers Union, Unite the Union) to block the lab from supplying technology to US and Israeli militaries. Move accelerated after Alphabet removed its public pledge against weapons development in February 2025. Google signed Pentagon deal allowing military use for 'any lawful government purpose.' DeepMind and OpenAI staff signed letter supporting Anthropic after DoD labeled it a supply chain risk for refusing autonomous weapons.

items.headline: Pentagon Expands AI Partnerships; Anthropic Contract Cancelled
items.summary: US Department of Defense signed agreements with Microsoft, Amazon, Nvidia, and Reflection AI for classified operations. Follows cancellation of $200M Anthropic contract over restrictions on domestic surveillance and autonomous weapons. Pentagon frames expansion as preventing vendor lock-in and building 'AI-first fighting force.' White House sources suggest administration may seek to bring Anthropic back; its Claude model remains in use across US security agencies.
